links.outcome: Physician clinical vignette performance with vs without GPT-4o access
links.effect: LLM access improved performance: Kenya 18% (95% CI 12.7 to 23.2), Indonesia 10.7% (5.7 to 15.7), Netherlands 7.2% (3.7 to 10.7), all p<0.001; some physicians without access outperformed those with access.
links.quote: Results showed that LLM access significantly improved clinical performance, with the largest effect in Kenya (18%, 95% CI: 12.7 to 23.2, p  < 0.001), followed by Indonesia (10.7%, 95% CI: 5.7 to 15.7, p  < 0.001) and the Netherlands (7.2%, 95% CI: 3.7 to 10.7, p  < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Providing physicians in low- and middle-income countries with LLM access to reduce cross-country disparities in care quality

screen.reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating the impact of providing physicians with LLM assistance (GPT-4o) versus standard care without LLM on clinical decision-making performance across clinical vignettes.
